children: European Central Bank policymakers expect to increase interest rates in December to fight high, energy-led inflation and then pause as a rise in bond yields is set to weigh on growth and inflation, three sources told Reuters.

The ECB left interest rates unchanged in a well-telegraphed move on Thursday and President Christine Lagarde hinted at another hike in December with a warning that high and rising energy costs were fuelling inflation risks.

Three policymakers who spoke to Reuters after the meeting said a hike on December 17, which would take the ECB's deposit rate to 2.75%, was all but certain, barring a sudden collapse in energy prices.

But they expected to hit the pause button thereafter, after ECB estimates circulated before Thursday's meeting showed that the recent increase in bond yields would lower economic growth by a cumulated 100 basis points and inflation by 90 basis points in 2027-28 compared to the September baseline projection.
An ECB spokesperson declined to comment.
